title: Revisiting Evaluation Metrics for Semantic Segmentation: Optimization and Evaluation of Fine-grained Intersection over Union
mechanism: Per-image and per-class-per-image mIoU plus worst-case (lowest k%) variants reduce bias to large objects and expose failure cases.
adaptation: Report per-cell crack and inactive IoU means and worst-10% next to dataset-level IoU so the 3 cells with 59% of inactive pixels cannot decide inactive; worst-case crack metric matches the 'almost all cracks' goal; mIoU over 24 classes computed per image ignores classes absent in a cell.
min_experiment: Arm: per-cell mean and worst-10% IoU on OOF predictions of house vs PF. Baseline: dataset-level IoU. Metric: paired-delta SE/|delta|. Kill: neither cuts that ratio by >= 20%.
evidence: R: 15 networks on 12 natural and aerial datasets; fine-grained mIoUs reduce large-object bias; architecture and loss choices change fine-grained ranking.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark: report pooled IoU plus per-cell IoU and worst-k cells per source; loss arm JML per-image vs per-batch.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: rescore val predictions of SUP100, PF, FINAL with per-cell and worst-k IoU; keep as secondary benchmark metrics if they reorder models or narrow CIs.
